external:core/assets/asset-union.json.description: Canonical union of all asset variant schemas. Referenced from creative-asset.json and creative-manifest.json to ensure a single named type is emitted by schema-to-TypeScript tooling. Add new asset types here and to the creative/asset-types registry.

external:core/assets/video-asset.json.title: Video Asset
external:core/assets/video-asset.json.description: A hosted video file delivered directly (e.g., an MP4 you host), with URL and technical specifications including audio track properties. `width` and `height` are required because a hosted video file has intrinsic, native pixel dimensions that are known when the file is created. Tag-delivered video uses the separate `vast` asset, which carries no `width`/`height`: a VAST response resolves geometry per-`MediaFile` at serve time, so there is no single width/height for the ad. Aspect-ratio and size *constraints* (what a placement accepts) belong on the format/requirements layer, not on the asset.
external:core/assets/video-asset.json.$comment: Dimension policy is deliberate and differs by asset type: a hosted `video` asset requires width/height (intrinsic pixels of a concrete file), while the `vast` asset omits them entirely (renditions are selected per-MediaFile by the player at serve time). Do not infer that AdCP forces a single width/height onto all video — only onto hosted files.

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as a video asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

url.description: URL to the video asset

width.description: Width in pixels — the video file's intrinsic native width. Required: a hosted file always has concrete dimensions. (Tag-delivered video carries no width; see the `vast` asset.)

height.description: Height in pixels — the video file's intrinsic native height. Required: a hosted file always has concrete dimensions. (Tag-delivered video carries no height; see the `vast` asset.)

container_format.description: Video container format (mp4, webm, mov, etc.)

video_codec.description: Video codec used (h264, h265, vp9, av1, prores, etc.)

video_bitrate_kbps.description: Video stream bitrate in kilobits per second

frame_rate.description: Frame rate as string to preserve precision (e.g., '23.976', '29.97', '30')

hdr_format.description: HDR format if applicable, or 'sdr' for standard dynamic range

has_audio.description: Whether the video contains an audio track

audio_codec.description: Audio codec used (aac, aac_lc, he_aac, pcm, mp3, ac3, eac3, etc.)

audio_bitrate_kbps.description: Audio bitrate in kilobits per second

captions_url.description: URL to captions file (WebVTT, SRT, etc.)

transcript_url.description: URL to text transcript of the video content

audio_description_url.description: URL to audio description track for visually impaired users

provenance.description: Provenance metadata for this asset, overrides manifest-level provenance

external:enums/frame-rate-type.json.title: Frame Rate Type
external:enums/frame-rate-type.json.description: Whether the video uses a constant or variable frame rate. Broadcast and SSAI contexts require constant frame rate for seamless splicing.

enumDescriptions.constant: Constant frame rate (CFR) — each frame occupies an identical time interval
enumDescriptions.variable: Variable frame rate (VFR) — frame intervals may differ

external:enums/scan-type.json.title: Scan Type
external:enums/scan-type.json.description: Video scan method. Modern digital delivery requires progressive scan; interlaced is retained for broadcast legacy content.

enumDescriptions.progressive: All lines of each frame are drawn in sequence
enumDescriptions.interlaced: Alternating lines drawn in two passes per frame (legacy broadcast)

external:enums/gop-type.json.title: GOP Type
external:enums/gop-type.json.description: Group of Pictures structure. SSAI and broadcast require closed GOPs for clean splice points; open GOPs may produce artifacts at ad boundaries.

enumDescriptions.closed: Each GOP is independently decodable — required for SSAI and broadcast splicing
enumDescriptions.open: GOPs may reference frames from adjacent GOPs — not suitable for splicing

external:enums/moov-atom-position.json.title: Moov Atom Position
external:enums/moov-atom-position.json.description: Position of the moov atom in an MP4 container. 'start' enables progressive download without buffering the entire file; required for streaming ad delivery.

enumDescriptions.start: moov atom at beginning of file — enables progressive download and streaming delivery
enumDescriptions.end: moov atom at end of file — requires full download before playback can begin

external:enums/audio-channel-layout.json.title: Audio Channel Layout
external:enums/audio-channel-layout.json.description: Audio channel configuration for audio and video assets

external:core/assets/audio-asset.json.title: Audio Asset
external:core/assets/audio-asset.json.description: Audio asset with URL and technical specifications

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as an audio asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

url.description: URL to the audio asset

container_format.description: Audio container/file format (mp3, m4a, aac, wav, ogg, flac, etc.)

codec.description: Audio codec used (aac, aac_lc, he_aac, pcm, mp3, vorbis, opus, flac, ac3, eac3, etc.)

transcript_url.description: URL to text transcript of the audio content

provenance.description: Provenance metadata for this asset, overrides manifest-level provenance

external:core/assets/vast-asset.json.title: VAST Asset
external:core/assets/vast-asset.json.description: VAST (Video Ad Serving Template) tag for third-party video or audio ad serving. Unlike a hosted media asset, a VAST tag carries no single `width`/`height`: a response can return multiple renditions and the player selects one at serve time. Standardized VAST audio support begins at 4.1 and uses MediaFile width and height values of 0; older audio-in-VAST versions are seller-declared legacy interoperability. Dimensional, duration, MIME-type, and codec constraints live on the format/requirements layer, not on this asset.

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as a VAST asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

vast_version.description: Exact VAST version declared by the supplied URL response or inline document. Required by the 3.2 canonical `video_vast` and `audio_vast` manifest paths; optional only on the deprecated named-format compatibility path. Receivers MUST NOT relabel or synthesize a newer version merely because the destination accepts it.

macro_declarations.description: One declaration per exact occurrence in a field carried by this asset. A URL-delivered asset can declare only occurrences in its locator `url`; tokens discovered later in a fetched VAST response require document validation evidence or an inline/snapshotted asset and MUST NOT be guessed from the locator. IAB tokens cite a registry namespace and revision rather than copying the live registry into AdCP.

vpaid_enabled.description: Whether VPAID (Video Player-Ad Interface Definition) is supported

duration_ms.description: Expected media duration in milliseconds (if known)

tracking_events.description: Tracking events supported by this VAST tag

captions_url.description: URL to captions file (WebVTT, SRT, etc.)

audio_description_url.description: URL to audio description track for visually impaired users

provenance.description: Provenance metadata for this asset, overrides manifest-level provenance

delivery_type.description: Discriminator indicating VAST is delivered via URL endpoint

url.description: URL endpoint returning VAST XML. Macro delimiters remain byte-preserved; declarations distinguish occurrences in this locator URL from occurrences in inline or fetched VAST content.

delivery_type.description: Discriminator indicating VAST is delivered as inline XML content

external:core/macro-declaration.json.title: Macro Declaration
external:core/macro-declaration.json.description: The source-faithful contract for one occurrence of one macro token. It identifies the current dialect, verified mapping status, exact asset-field occurrence, next processing operation, actor, and encoding. Translation and concrete value resolution are separate operations: a translator emits the declared native token and replaces this declaration with the target declaration. Unknown tokens are always byte-preserved.

verifier_constraints.adcp_semantic_identity: when dialect is adcp, dialect_semantic must equal universal_semantic
verifier_constraints.declaration_id_uniqueness: declaration_id must be unique within the containing asset
verifier_constraints.token_occurrence: location must identify the declared zero-based occurrence of token in location.field
verifier_constraints.asset_field: location.field must exist on and be permitted by the containing asset type
verifier_constraints.catalog_universal_profile: catalog semantics require seller resolve_value in a URL context with exactly one rfc3986 pass
verifier_constraints.omit_parameter_scope: omit_parameter requires the token to occupy the complete URL query-parameter value

declaration_id.description: Identifier unique within the enclosing asset, used to correlate validation results.

token.description: Exact byte-preserved token expression at this occurrence, including delimiters.

dialect_namespace.description: Authority-controlled registry or mapping URI. Required for IAB VAST, IAB DAAST, and vendor dialects.

dialect_revision.description: Immutable registry/mapping revision, release, commit, or digest. Required for IAB VAST, IAB DAAST, and vendor dialects.

dialect_semantic.description: Exact semantic identifier in the cited dialect, such as `CACHEBUSTING`, `PLAYERSTATE`, or a documented vendor name. This is not inferred from token spelling.

universal_semantic.description: Verified AdCP universal meaning. Present only when mapping_status is `verified_universal`.

performed_by.description: Actor authorized to perform the declared translation or value resolution. Omitted for preservation.

translation_target.description: Required only for `translate_to_native`. The output token contract that replaces this declaration after translation.

occurrence.description: Zero-based occurrence of this exact token within the named field.

encoding.description: Encoding for the concrete value. Translation/preservation uses `none` at depth zero.

required.description: Whether terminal delivery must fail if the declared operation cannot complete.

unavailable_behavior.description: Action when the responsible actor has no value. Omission is legal only for a complete URL query-value occurrence; dialect sentinels require a cited dialect rule.

external:enums/macro-dialect.json.title: Macro Dialect Family
external:enums/macro-dialect.json.description: Governed family for a creative macro token. `vendor` is qualified by an authority-controlled namespace and immutable revision on the declaration/capability; AdCP does not enumerate companies as dialects. `unknown` is declaration-only and always byte-preserved.

enumDescriptions.adcp: AdCP universal macro syntax and semantics.
enumDescriptions.iab_vast: IAB VAST macro syntax, qualified by the referenced live-registry revision.
enumDescriptions.iab_daast: IAB DAAST macro syntax, qualified by the referenced specification/registry revision.
enumDescriptions.vendor: A vendor- or platform-owned macro namespace, qualified by its authoritative URI and immutable revision.
enumDescriptions.unknown: The token namespace cannot be established. Preserve the token unchanged and never advertise it as resolvable.

external:enums/macro-mapping-status.json.title: Macro Mapping Status
external:enums/macro-mapping-status.json.description: Evidence level connecting a dialect-local macro meaning to the AdCP universal vocabulary.

enumDescriptions.verified_universal: The cited dialect mapping verifies an AdCP universal semantic.
enumDescriptions.dialect_defined: The dialect defines the token, but no AdCP universal semantic is asserted.
enumDescriptions.unresolved: No safe meaning is established; the token remains byte-preserved.

external:enums/universal-macro.json.title: Universal Macro
external:enums/universal-macro.json.description: Standardized macro placeholders for dynamic value substitution in creative tracking URLs. Macros are replaced with actual values at impression time. See docs/creative/universal-macros.mdx for detailed documentation.

enumDescriptions.CLICK_URL: Publisher's click tracking URL (auto-inserted by sales agent)
enumDescriptions.GPP_SID: GPP Section ID(s) indicating applicable privacy framework sections
enumDescriptions.IP_ADDRESS: User IP address (often masked for privacy, may return empty)
enumDescriptions.DEVICE_TYPE: Device category (mobile, tablet, desktop, ctv, dooh)
enumDescriptions.OS: Operating system (iOS, Android, tvOS, Roku, etc.)
enumDescriptions.POD_SIZE: Total ads in the ad break
enumDescriptions.INSTALLMENT_ID: Installment identifier (podcast episode, print issue, etc.)
enumDescriptions.TMPX: TMP exposure token — HPKE-encrypted identity tokens for per-user exposure tracking. Produced by Identity Match, substituted into creative tracking URLs, received by the buyer's impression pixel.
enumDescriptions.IMPRESSION_ID: Opaque, collision-resistant identifier for one impression opportunity. Used for impression deduplication, cross-vendor reconciliation, pixel-retry dedup, and TMP cross-identity exposure dedup. Minted by the publisher, ad-decision layer, or buyer at {TMPX} decode; required upstream for TMP context-only impressions where {TMPX} is absent.
enumDescriptions.AXEM: AXE contextual metadata (encoded blob). Legacy — in TMP, use Offer creative_data for dynamic creative values and TMPX for exposure tracking.
enumDescriptions.CATALOG_ID: Buyer-defined catalog identifier from the catalog's catalog_id field
enumDescriptions.SKU: Product SKU identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.GTIN: Global Trade Item Number for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.OFFERING_ID: AdCP offering identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.JOB_ID: Job posting identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.HOTEL_ID: Hotel property identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.FLIGHT_ID: Flight route identifier for the catalog item being rendered

external:enums/vast-tracking-event.json.title: VAST Tracking Event
external:enums/vast-tracking-event.json.description: Tracking events for VAST video and audio ads. Includes the IAB VAST 4.2 `Tracking@event` enumeration (vast_4.2.xsd `TrackingEvents_type`, lines 112–136), plus AdCP-flattened representations of the `Impression`, `Error`, `VideoClicks`, and `ViewableImpression` elements (which live in dedicated VAST elements, not under `<TrackingEvents>` — they are surfaced here so a single declared list can cover everything a measurement vendor wants to track). Audio players execute only events applicable to and present in the audio VAST document; visual viewability, fullscreen, expand, collapse, and interactive events are not implied by `audio_vast`. `fullscreen` / `exitFullscreen` are retained for VAST 2.x / 3.x video compatibility (VAST 4.0+ replaced them with `playerExpand` / `playerCollapse`). `measurableImpression` is an AdCP extension for MRC measurability signals.

external:core/macro-bearing-url.json.title: Macro-bearing URL

Macro-bearing HTTP(S) URLs require a valid lexical authority and valid percent triplets; an AdCP verifier replaces each recognized token with an unreserved sentinel and validates the resulting absolute URI. Token semantics are established only by `macro_declarations`.

verifier_constraints.macro_aware_uri: mask recognized token lexical forms with an RFC3986 unreserved sentinel, whether declared or on the undeclared 3.x compatibility path, then require a valid absolute HTTP or HTTPS URI; masking assigns no semantics

external:enums/daast-tracking-event.json.title: DAAST Tracking Event
external:enums/daast-tracking-event.json.description: Tracking events for audio ads. Aligned to the IAB DAAST 1.1 `Tracking@event` enumeration from §3.2.1.7 of the spec (creativeView, start, firstQuartile, midpoint, thirdQuartile, complete, mute, unmute, pause, rewind, resume, skip, progress) — plus `close` (referenced descriptively in DAAST 1.1 §3.2.4.2 contrasting it with `skip`), and AdCP-flattened representations of the `Impression`, `Error`, and click elements (`<Impression>`, `<Error>`, and the click children of `<AdInteractions>`) so a single declared list can cover everything a measurement vendor wants to track. `viewable` / `notViewable` / `viewUndetermined` and `measurableImpression` / `viewableImpression` are AdCP extensions for OM-SDK Audio measurability signals (DAAST 1.1 itself does not define a `<ViewableImpression>` element). DAAST 1.1 audio-incompatible video events are deliberately omitted: no `loaded`, `playerExpand` / `playerCollapse`, `fullscreen` / `exitFullscreen`, `acceptInvitation`, `adExpand` / `adCollapse`, `minimize`, `overlayViewDuration`, or `interactiveStart`.

external:core/catalog.json.title: Catalog
external:core/catalog.json.description: A typed data feed. Catalogs carry the items, locations, stock levels, or pricing that publishers use to render ads. They can be synced to a platform via sync_catalogs (managed lifecycle with approval), provided inline, or fetched from an external URL. The catalog type determines the item schema and can be structural (offering, product, inventory, store, promotion) or vertical-specific (hotel, flight, job, vehicle, real_estate, education, destination, app). Selectors (ids, tags, category, query) filter items regardless of sourcing method.

catalog_id.description: Buyer's identifier for this catalog. Required when syncing via sync_catalogs. When used in creatives, references a previously synced catalog on the account.

name.description: Human-readable name for this catalog (e.g., 'Summer Products 2025', 'Amsterdam Store Locations').

type.description: Catalog type. Structural types: 'offering' (AdCP Offering objects), 'product' (ecommerce entries), 'inventory' (stock per location), 'store' (physical locations), 'promotion' (deals and pricing). Vertical types: 'hotel', 'flight', 'job', 'vehicle', 'real_estate', 'education', 'destination', 'app' — each with an industry-specific item schema.

url.description: URL to an external catalog feed. The platform fetches and resolves items from this URL. For offering-type catalogs, the feed contains an array of Offering objects. For other types, the feed format is determined by feed_format. When omitted with type 'product', the platform uses its synced copy of the brand's product catalog.

feed_format.description: Format of the external feed at url. Required when url points to a non-AdCP feed (e.g., Google Merchant Center XML, Meta Product Catalog). Omit for offering-type catalogs where the feed is native AdCP JSON.

update_frequency.description: How often the platform should re-fetch the feed from url. Only applicable when url is provided. Platforms may use this as a hint for polling schedules.

items.description: Inline catalog data. The item schema depends on the catalog type: Offering objects for 'offering', StoreItem for 'store', HotelItem for 'hotel', FlightItem for 'flight', JobItem for 'job', VehicleItem for 'vehicle', RealEstateItem for 'real_estate', EducationItem for 'education', DestinationItem for 'destination', AppItem for 'app', or freeform objects for 'product', 'inventory', and 'promotion'. Mutually exclusive with url — provide one or the other, not both. Implementations should validate items against the type-specific schema.

ids.description: Filter catalog to exact canonical item keys. The key field is offering_id for offering, store_id for store, hotel_id for hotel, flight_id for flight, job_id for job, vehicle_id for vehicle, listing_id for real_estate, program_id for education, destination_id for destination, and app_id for app. Product, inventory, and promotion catalogs use the stable normalized source identifier retained during ingestion (for example a retailer SKU). The same canonical key is used by catalog availability item_id.

gtins.description: Filter product-type catalogs by GTIN identifiers for cross-retailer catalog matching. Accepts standard GTIN formats (GTIN-8, UPC-A/GTIN-12, EAN-13/GTIN-13, GTIN-14). Only applicable when type is 'product'.

tags.description: Filter catalog to items with these tags. Tags are matched using OR logic — items matching any tag are included.

category.description: Filter catalog to items in this category (e.g., 'beverages/soft-drinks', 'chef-positions').

query.description: Natural language filter for catalog items (e.g., 'all pasta sauces under $5', 'amsterdam vacancies').

conversion_events.description: Event types that represent conversions for items in this catalog. Declares what events the platform should attribute to catalog items — e.g., a job catalog converts via submit_application, a product catalog via purchase. The event's content_ids field carries the item IDs that connect back to catalog items. Use content_id_type to declare what identifier type content_ids values represent.

content_id_type.description: Identifier type that the event's content_ids field should be matched against for items in this catalog. For example, 'gtin' means content_ids values are Global Trade Item Numbers, 'sku' means retailer SKUs. Omit when using a custom identifier scheme not listed in the enum.

feed_field_mappings.description: Declarative normalization rules for external feeds. Maps non-standard feed field names, date formats, price encodings, and image URLs to the AdCP catalog item schema. Applied during sync_catalogs ingestion. Supports field renames, named transforms (date, divide, boolean, split), static literal injection, and assignment of image URLs to typed asset pools.

external:enums/catalog-type.json.title: Catalog Type
external:enums/catalog-type.json.description: The type of catalog feed. Determines the item schema and how the platform resolves catalog items. Multiple catalog types can be synced to the same account and referenced together in creatives.

external:enums/feed-format.json.title: Feed Format
external:enums/feed-format.json.description: Catalog feed formats. Determines how the platform (seller) parses items from an external feed URL. Each named value is an externally-documented feed specification a seller parses natively without buyer-supplied feed_field_mappings; values are vendor spec names (proper nouns), not semantic categories. Use `custom` + feed_field_mappings for any feed whose shape is not one of the named formats.

enumDescriptions.google_merchant_center: Google Merchant Center / Google Shopping product data specification — the de-facto e-commerce product-feed lingua franca that the other named commerce formats derive from.
enumDescriptions.facebook_catalog: Meta (Facebook / Instagram) product catalog feed — a Google-Merchant-Center-derived dialect, the closest clone of the GMC field set.
enumDescriptions.tiktok_shop: TikTok Shop product catalog feed — a GMC-derived dialect with material deltas (sku_id as the primary identifier rather than id, and a first-class video_link) that a GMC parser keyed on id would mis-parse.
enumDescriptions.pinterest_catalog: Pinterest product catalog feed — a GMC-derived dialect with stricter serialization (composite-encoded price and shipping, a mandatory google_product_category, space-delimited availability enums) that a strict GMC parser would mis-handle.
enumDescriptions.openai_product_feed: OpenAI Commerce product feed for ChatGPT shopping — a GMC-derived dialect adding ChatGPT-specific eligibility flags (is_eligible_search / is_eligible_checkout / is_eligible_ads). Spec: https://developers.openai.com/commerce/specs/file-upload/products
enumDescriptions.custom: A feed whose shape is not one of the named formats above. The buyer MUST supply feed_field_mappings to normalize it to the AdCP catalog item schema.
